segments.text: You type in the exact right prompt and out pops the perfect answer.
But think back to the best history class project you ever worked on.
Your group didn't start with a flawless finished product.
You shared ideas, figured out what was missing,
and improved the work as a team.
That is exactly how you should work with AI.
It is a two-person team, just you and the AI,
and getting the best result takes a back-and-forth conversation over several rounds.
The first move is to treat AI as a thought partner.
You can ask each other questions and bounce ideas around,
keeping in mind that you always make the final decisions.
Let's look at this board showing a conversation about starting a summer business.
Here, the student says,
I'd like to earn money this summer by starting a small business.
Can we talk through what might fit me?
Instead of just giving a generic list, the AI answers,
what are you already good at and what problems do people around you
regularly need help solving?
The student replies,
I'm good with dogs and teaching younger kids math.
Now the AI has enough context to answer.
That gives us three realistic directions,
pet care, math tutoring, and a neighborhood errand service,
which sounds most interesting to you and which would be easiest to start.
Notice how the AI gathers information to understand your situation
before it offers solutions.
A good conversation asks about you before it answers.
The second move is to use AI as a learning tool when a concept doesn't make sense.
To do this effectively, ask follow-up questions,
connect the new idea to something you already know,
check your understanding,
and then try explaining it back to the AI in your own words.
This graphic shows how that works in practice.
The student sets up a familiar scenario.
I might start a business this summer mowing lawns.
What is profit and how do I calculate it?
Explain it using simple numbers that apply to a lawn mowing business.
The AI answers,
profit is the money left after you subtract every cost from your sales.
For example, your sales are $300.
Your total costs are $150, leaving you with $150 in profit.
The formula is sales minus costs equals profit.
By forcing the AI to ground its explanation in a context you already understand,
the math becomes clear.
Ask AI to explain the idea using a situation you know.
The third move helps when you face a massive decision
and suffer from blank page paralysis,
where you don't even know where to begin.
This board shows how to break that paralysis.
The student sets clear boundaries.
I need to start thinking about college, but I don't know where to begin.
Ask me one question at a time to help me figure out what matters to me.
Don't recommend a college yet.
The AI provides a single guiding question.
Do you already have a career or field in mind?
Or do you want college to help you explore different possibilities?
Turning a huge decision into a single initial question
creates an actionable starting point.
When you don't know where to begin, ask AI for the first question.
The final concept is iteration.
To iterate means to build something inversions
using each version to improve the next.
This board shows the difference iteration makes.
Look at this vague early round prompt.
Give me ideas for a summer business.
The AI gives a generic response.
Here are some ideas.
Lawn care, pet sitting, tutoring, car washing, and selling crafts online.
Now look at a later round where the student provides detailed parameters.
I'm considering a lawn cutting business.
I'll serve homes within biking distance, use the customer's mower,
work weekday afternoons, and charge by lawn size.
Help me find weaknesses in the plan and improve it.
Because the AI has specific details, it can offer a rigorous pressure test.
Let's pressure test it.
How will you quote lawn sizes?
What happens when it rains?
The AI can only refine your work
if you provide it with specific parameters to test against.
Better details give AI better material to improve.
The next level starts after the first answer.
Explore ideas, build understanding, and improve together.
